title: Count sparse trimmed fibers with projected boxes

add.label: Fiber counting
add.name: Fiber counting by free coordinates
add.statement: For any rank-$d$ lattice $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb Z^I$ with basis matrix $B$ and the uniform box sampler on $\{2,\ldots,g+1\}^I$, its largest fiber density is at most $g^{-d}$. For every stack $\mathbf W$ with either sampler, $\operatorname{gp}(\mathbf W)\le g^{-\operatorname{rank}\mathbf W}$, and $\operatorname{gp}(v^\top)\ge\operatorname{gp}(\mathbf W)$ for each vector $v$ in its row space. In the lattice case let $A=B^\top$. In the stack case let $A$ be the vertical concatenation of the $W_c$, omitting column $0$ if it is zero. In each case the retained tuple consists of the sampled coordinates indexed by the columns of $A$, with original indices. Write $m$ for the number of retained coordinates.
add.proof:
In the centered sampler, given the positive-index draws, $r_0$ is uniform on $g$ consecutive integers because its defining formula translates the independent uniform $r_\star$.
Every list of $g$ consecutive integers has distinct residues modulo $q$ because $g<q$.
The product rule for probabilities gives each retained tuple in the support mass $g^{-m}$, using the uniform positive-index draws and the uniform conditional law at index $0$ whenever retained.
Choose $\operatorname{rank} A$ independent columns, including column $0$ whenever retained in the stack case.
On any fiber of $A$ the chosen coordinates are determined by the other coordinates by linear independence of the chosen columns.
The other coordinates have at most $g^{m-\operatorname{rank} A}$ tuples because each ranges over $\{2,\ldots,g+1\}$.
Dividing by $g^m$ bounds the mass of each fiber by $g^{-\operatorname{rank} A}$.
For a vector $v$ in the stack row space, $v^\top r$ is a linear image of the stack output.
The image of a most probable stack output has probability at least that output's probability.
add.explain: The lattice and stack bounds both count the free coordinates of a fiber.

add.label: Witness from a tied tensor
add.name: A tied low-rank passing stack supplies a witness
add.statement: Every nonzero usable stack of rank at most three whose row space contains no kernel vector has a witness of $S$ in its row space.
add.proof:
Work over $K=\mathbb F_{q^n}$, with $a=n/2-1$, $b=n/2$, $c=n/2+1$ and $I=\{a,b,c\}$.
Set $(Z_a,Z_b,Z_c)=(W_U,W_V,\sigma^c(W_U))$.
Writing $z_s=\sigma^s(z)$, the three defining tie polynomials reduce modulo $P$ to $Z_s z_t-Z_t z_s$ for the pairs $(a,b),(a,c),(b,c)$ by the substitution action of $\sigma$.
Thus $Z_s z_t=Z_t z_s$ for all three pairs.
Choose a basis matrix $B$ for the row space $\mathcal V$ of dimension $d$, and write its rows as $u_i^\top$.
As linear combinations of symmetric stack matrices, the $Z_s$ have both row and column spaces in the extension of $\mathcal V$.
Take a base-field left inverse $C$ of $B$ and set $M_s=C Z_s C^\top$.
Then $B M_s B^\top=Z_s$ because the projection $BC$ fixes the row and column spaces of $Z_s$.
At least one of $M_a,M_b$ is nonzero since recovering $Z_a,Z_b$ by this factorization recovers all stack coefficients.
Let $h_s=B^\top z_s$ for all $s$.
Since $B$ has base-field entries, $h_s=\sigma^s(h_0)$.
The entries of $h_0$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb F_q$ since a relation on them gives a vector of $\mathcal V$ in the kernel of $z$.
The entries of $h_a$ remain independent over $\mathbb F_q$ since $\sigma^a$ is an automorphism fixing the base field.
The Moore determinant demand makes the first $d$ of $h_a,h_b,h_c$ a basis, as its matrix has the successive Frobenius powers of the entries of $h_a$ as its rows.
By injectivity of $B$, the reduced ties give $M_s h_t=M_t h_s$.
For a relation $\sum_{s\in I} \lambda_s h_s=0$, the ties give $(\sum_s \lambda_s M_s) h_t=M_t\sum_s \lambda_s h_s=0$ for each $t$.
The spanning property then gives $\sum_s \lambda_s M_s=0$.
Consequently $h_s\mapsto M_s$ defines a linear map $M$.
The trilinear form $L(x,y,z')=y^\top M(x)z'$ is symmetric in its last two arguments by symmetry of the matrices.
Extending the reduced ties by bilinearity gives $M(x)z^{\prime}=M(z^{\prime})x$ for all $x,z^{\prime}$.
For each $i>0$ the Booleanity test yields $L(h_s,u_i,u_i-u_0)=0$ since it holds on the linear combination of stack matrices $Z_s$.
By spanning, $L(x,u_i,u_i-u_0)=0$ for every $x$.
Also $Z_a=\sigma^a(Z_c)$ by $a+c=n$.
Since $Z_b=W_V$ only has even powers of $T$, $\sigma^b(Z_b)=Z_b$ by $\omega^b=-1$.
Applying $Z\mapsto C Z C^\top$ over the base field gives $M_s=\sigma^s(M_{n-s})$ for $s=a,b$.
Suppose first that $u_0=0$ and choose a basis $(l_1,\ldots,l_d)$ from the rows $u_i$.
The Booleanity identities give $L(x,l_i,l_i)=0$ for all $x$ in this case.
By symmetry, all tensor coordinates with a repeated index vanish.
If $d<3$ there are no other coordinates, so $L=0$.
For $d=3$ the off-diagonal entries of $M_s$ on basis pairs are $t=L(l_1,l_2,l_3)$ times the coordinate of $h_s$ in the complementary slot, by symmetry.
Comparing those coordinates in $M_s=\sigma^s(M_{n-s})$ gives $t h_s=\sigma^s(t)h_0$ for $s=a,b$.
Independence of $h_a,h_b$ in dimension three forces $t=0$ by these equations.
So $L=0$ also in dimension three.
The zero form is impossible since at least one of $M_a,M_b$ is nonzero, so $u_0\ne0$.
Extend $l_0=u_0$ to a basis using rows $l_i=u_{j_i}$ for $1\le i<d$.
For $\delta\in\{0,1\}^{d-1}$ define $p_\delta$ by $l_0^\top p_\delta=1$ and $l_i^\top p_\delta=\delta_i$, and set $w_\delta=B p_\delta$.
For $i>0$ the Booleanity identities give $L(x,l_i,l_i)=L(x,l_i,l_0)$.
By symmetry and these reductions, each tensor coordinate depends only on the set of positive indices it contains.
On the Boolean cube the squarefree monomials are a basis of functions by triangularity under subset inclusion.
The form $(x,y,z^{\prime})\mapsto(x^\top p_\delta)(y^\top p_\delta)(z^{\prime}^\top p_\delta)$ has coordinate $\prod_{i\in A}\delta_i$ at a basis triple with positive index set $A$.
Thus these forms span the tensors with the stated coordinates by invertibility of the evaluation matrix.
Write $M(x)=\sum_\delta C_\delta (x^\top p_\delta)p_\delta p_\delta^\top$ using this expansion.
The matrices $p_\delta p_\delta^\top$ are independent since their evaluations on pairs of basis rows give all the same squarefree monomials for $d-1\le 2$.
Put $z_\delta=h_0^\top p_\delta$, which is nonzero since $w_\delta$ has coordinate zero equal to $1$ and $\mathcal V$ has no kernel vector.
Comparing coefficients in $M_s=\sigma^s(M_{n-s})$ now gives $C_\delta\sigma^s(z_\delta)=\sigma^s(C_\delta) z_\delta$ for $s=a,b$.
Dividing the coefficient equations gives $x_\delta=\sigma^a(x_\delta)=\sigma^b(x_\delta)$ for $x_\delta=C_\delta/z_\delta$.
Applying $\sigma^{-a}$ to $\sigma^a(x_\delta)=\sigma^b(x_\delta)$ gives $x_\delta=\sigma(x_\delta)$.
Write $\chi_\delta=C_\delta/z_\delta\in\mathbb F_q$ by the fixed field of Frobenius.
Any linear test $\varrho$ with base-field coefficients vanishes on $Z_a,Z_b,Z_c$ because it vanishes on every stack entry.
The resulting equations are $h_0^\top A_\varrho h_s=0$ for $s=a,b,c$, with $A_\varrho=\sum_\delta\chi_\delta\varrho(w_\delta w_\delta^\top)p_\delta p_\delta^\top$ by the expansion.
Spanning gives $h_0^\top A_\varrho=0$.
The base-field entries of $A_\varrho$ and independence of the entries of $h_0$ give $A_\varrho=0$.
Independence of the squares gives $\chi_\delta\varrho(w_\delta w_\delta^\top)=0$ for every $\delta$.
Some $\chi_\delta$ is nonzero since otherwise the expansion gives $M=0$.
For that $\delta$, dividing the test equations by $\chi_\delta$ gives $\varrho(w_\delta w_\delta^\top)=0$ for every test.
The Booleanity tests force $(w_\delta)_i\in\{0,1\}$ since they give $(w_\delta)_i^2=(w_\delta)_i$.
The constraint tests certify that this Boolean assignment in $\mathcal V$ is a witness because each term $a^\top(w_\delta w_\delta^\top)b$ evaluates to the corresponding product $(a^\top w_\delta)(b^\top w_\delta)$.
add.explain: Use the test contractions of the tied tensor to find one Boolean point satisfying the constraints.

add.label: Zero stacks for the target pair
add.name: The difference of the two received target expressions has zero stacks
add.statement: The difference $G_T-\mathsf K^\alpha$ of the two received target-group expressions has zero stacks in both sectors.
add.proof: Every stack entry of this difference is zero by definition, since its only nonzero pairing coefficient is indexed by $(G_1,G_2)$ rather than a left-factor and right-factor pair.
add.explain: Use the view result for a zero-stack difference rather than deducing nonidentity from variation of a sampled exponent.

add.label: Packing a short kernel multiple
add.name: A short kernel multiple yields a packed Module-SIS solution
add.statement: Let $v\in\mathbb F_q^{N+1}$ be a nonzero kernel vector with $v_0=0$ and $x\in\mathbb Z^{N+1}$ a short multiple, so $x\equiv c v\pmod q$ for a nonzero $c\in\mathbb F_q$ and $\|x\|_\infty\le\beta$. Let $A$ be columns $1,\ldots,\ell$ of $M$. Form $\hat x\in R^\ell$ by the coefficient packing of the forms with integer entries. Then $A\hat x=0\pmod q$ and $0<\|\hat x\|_\infty\le\beta$.
add.proof:
With $v_0=0$, the defining coefficient blocks of $z(v)=0$ are those of $A\hat v$, where $\hat v$ is the packing over $R_q$.
By linearity of $x\mapsto A\hat x\bmod q$, $A\hat x\equiv c A\hat v=0\pmod q$.
The coefficients of $\hat x$ are positive-index entries of $x$ or padding zeros, so the sup norm is at most $\beta$.
At least one of these coefficients is nonzero modulo $q$ because $cv\ne0$ has zeroth coordinate zero.
add.explain: Prove the ring equation and norm guarantees as a counted result.

add.label: Reduction circuit cost
add.name: Time bound by evaluating and differentiating circuits
add.statement: Under the extraction theorem's hypotheses, if the adversary runs in time $t$ with at most $Q$ generic group calls and $Q_H$ queries to each random oracle, both $\mathcal B_0,\mathcal B_1$ run within $t_R=t+O(Q+d_R Q_H+\mu)+\mathsf{poly}(D,\log q)$ in the specified operations model including description and advice.
add.proof:
Sample the points of (R2) before the interaction, using their independence from the run.
Sampling the tuples costs polynomial time in $D$ by the stated lists of independent coordinates and the finite-set sampling operation.
The sampler $\mathcal D_g$ draws the encryption search vector in $O(N+1)$ operations by $N+1$ draws and integer sums and halving to center coordinate zero.
The bounds $N,n\le D$, $n=(k+1)d_R$ and $\ell=\lceil N/d_R\rceil$ bound all dimensions of the challenge matrix and the forms by $O(D)$.
The bound $K_1K_2=n/2$ bounds both leg counts and the cell count by $O(D)$.
Condition (P1) bounds $J,\Delta$ by $2D$.
The remainder definitions give $J'\le\max(1,n_{\mathsf c})$ and $\Delta'\le D$.
The published list has length polynomial in $D$ since its indices run through those ranges and the $N+1$ coordinates.
The exponent formulas take polynomial time in $D,\log q$ by Horner evaluation and polynomial arithmetic at the fixed number of encryption, private and recovery points.
In particular the fixed QAP polynomials can be stored as advice using $O(ND+D)$ field elements by their coefficient lists.
Programming the $k\ell$ challenge entries costs polynomial time in $D$.
The fixed message and its masking take $O(\mu)$ additional description and operations by writing it and applying XOR in label-sized blocks.
For each group store the partial injection in both directions and keep a table of strings excluded from future assignments.
Conditioned on the table, the injection on unassigned exponents is uniform among injections into the undecided strings.
A new exponent's label can therefore be drawn by the permitted uniform sample outside the excluded keys.
For an undecided operand string, the probability of a preimage is the number of unassigned exponents divided by the number of undecided strings.
Implement this probability by a uniform integer draw from $[0,U-1]$ compared with the number of unassigned exponents, where $U$ is the undecided count after the generators have labels.
Given membership, sample its exponent uniformly outside the assigned keys.
Initialize the ciphertext and key labels by applying the new-exponent rule at most once per published element plus the key.
One eligibility flag per target-group label implements the name-query restriction with constant updates per call.
The allowed table updates, group exponent arithmetic and name formation give constant overhead per generic group call, including failures.
Answer a fresh seed query by sampling the $d_R$ coefficients of its ring entry.
Answer a fresh key query by one sample from its prescribed finite range.
The oracle tables use $O(d_R Q_H)$ total operations by $d_R\ge 1$.
Implement each record by a reference to a scalar circuit over the received exponents.
Assign the zero circuit to any operand lacking a record, as prescribed.
Each group result's record adds a constant number of arithmetic gates because its exponent operation is linear or is a pairing product.
The extra subtraction in (R3) leaves $O(Q+1)$ gates beyond the received leaves.
Evaluating each new gate at the private point as it is added permits each comparison in (R3) in constant time.
Retain two pointers at the first discrepancy so that its selected difference takes one subtraction node.
Find the other selected record by one lookup at the target label.
For a recovery sector set the received leaves from the other sector of $\mathbb G_2$ and $\mathbb G_T$ to zero, with $G_2,G_T$ assigned to the plain sector.
By the target expression formula, which is linear in the right and key leaves, this substitution retains exactly the chosen sector.
The exponent evaluation circuits in the input $r$ have polynomial size in $D,\log q$ by the same arithmetic bounds.
By the gradient-cost demand, differentiating the full circuit in $r$ costs $O(Q)+\mathsf{poly}(D,\log q)$ per record and point.
For each sector, Gaussian elimination projects the linear system $v=\sum_l a_l g_l$, $\varphi_e(v)=0$ onto the coordinates of $v$, where $g_l$ are its three gradients and $a_l$ are scalar unknowns.
Finding a nonzero solution projected onto $v$ if one exists takes $\mathsf{poly}(D,\log q)$ operations by the dimensions $n,N+1$ and three.
There are at most two lifting calls, each polynomial in $N,\log q$ by the lifting demand.
Packing the result is polynomial in $D,\log q$ because there are $\ell$ polynomials of degree below $d_R$.
Adding the costs to $t$, with at most six gradient computations per selected expression and at most two expressions, gives $t_R=t+O(Q+d_R Q_H+\mu)+\mathsf{poly}(D,\log q)$.
add.explain: Bound the reduction by the circuit size and the total number of oracle operations.

add.label: Charged and guessed first marks
add.name: First-mark bounds with a shared message-mask coupling
add.statement: In an extraction run with either fixed challenge message, with the admissible parameters and the stated caps $Q<2^\lambda$ and $Q_H\le2^\lambda$, let $u=2Q+2$, $\varpi=\Omega_{22}\zeta\zeta^{\prime}\zeta^{\prime\prime}\varepsilon$, and $d_f=3D+2n+2K_1+6$. Each run that reaches a target query has a first mark, and each first mark is $\mathsf{init}$, $\mathsf{guess}$, charged, or good. The probability of a charged first mark is at most $N_{\mathrm{cmp}}(u)(\theta+\varepsilon_f)+(\binom{L+3u}{2}+L+3u)\varepsilon_f$. The probability that the first mark is $\mathsf{guess}$ is at most $2^\lambda/N_{\mathsf{free}}$.
add.proof:
Truncating before an excess call enforces the caps while preserving the extraction runs, which meet those caps by hypothesis.
By (M4) a target query sets a mark if a mark has not been set before it.
The assignments of marks in (M1)–(M4) and the definitions of goodness and charge give the stated four categories.
Given the encryption randomness and injections, the key oracle's value at the target string is a uniform message-length string independent of its values at other strings.
Hence the real run can be sampled by using a uniform mask $h$ and setting that one key answer to $h\oplus m$.
Changing that answer leaves the transcript through the first target query, before its answer, fixed.
The first mark has the same law in $\mathsf R_\$$ because (M1)–(M4) only inspect this prefix, or the whole run if there is no target query.
By (P2) each group has more than $L+3Q$ labels, enough for the symbolic assignments.
The lazy-label simulation demand couples this run with the symbolic run through the requests before a first collision.
In this coupling entries that do not collide have the exponents of their assigned labels as their evaluated values.
The symbolic transcript is independent of the exponent evaluation because it uses only formal expressions, label images, and the independently sampled mask and oracle answers.
On a charged-first-mark run there was no collision on received elements since (M1) would mark it $\mathsf{init}$.
If the first collision occurs before a target query, its later entry cannot be a fresh guess in a good collision, because that guess appears in the difference.
A good collision at a result merges it with the earlier entry's label in the real run by equality of exponents.
A good merge would set a good first mark by (M3), contradicting the charged mark.
If the query precedes the collision, the target label must have an entry since otherwise (M4) would give $\mathsf{guess}$.
It is a key-value entry in the evaluation by the coupling.
This entry must be bad since a good key-value entry would give a good mark by (M4).
For a fixed symbolic comparison difference or key-value expression containing guesses, the linear and bilinear expression forms make each nonconstant guess-monomial coefficient a constant or a source-group expression.
Since the charged bound is at least one when $\varepsilon_f\ge1$, in the charged analysis we may take $\varepsilon_f<1$.
For every fixed $r$, some formally nonzero guess coefficient is nonzero on the valid coins, by the collision demand for groups 1 and 2 if it is not a constant.
The cleared polynomial is nonzero because this guess coefficient is nonzero at some valid coins, where $\varpi\ne0$.
Each term linear in guesses has cleared total degree at most $d_f+1$ by the degree bound for groups 1 and 2 for its coefficient.
Each term in two guesses has cleared degree at most seven because its coefficient is constant and $\varpi$ has degree five.
Each independent evaluation coordinate has at least $q-D$ choices since the sampler excludes at most $\max(D,K_1+1)=D$, with $K_1\le n/2$ and $2\le n\le D$.
Applying the random evaluation bound at degree $d_f+1$ gives probability at most $(d_f+1)/(q-D)\le\varepsilon_f$, since the term without guesses has degree at most $d_f$.
With no guess variable, the view demands bound coincidence probability by $\varepsilon_f$ for each source-group comparison or target-group nonidentity at fixed $r$.
At an identity the mark stack is nonzero by the view demand for a formally distinct pair or a key comparison.
A bad event with an identity requires a light mark stack by definition.
All $r$ giving that identity are in a single fiber of the mark stack by the view demand.
The measure of this fiber is at most $\theta$ for a light stack, by the definition of guessing probability.
Thus each event without guess variables has bad-event probability at most $\theta+\varepsilon_f$.
Each call can introduce at most two guessed operands and one result into the tables.
The events with guess variables number at most $\binom{L+3Q}{2}+L+3Q$ by counting all unordered entry pairs and all single entries.
A collision without guess variables must have a result as its later entry unless both entries were received.
Only collisions after receipt matter here because an initial collision prevents a charged first mark.
Thus at call $j$ there are at most $L+3j-1$ earlier entries that could pair with its result.
A key value without guesses has at most $Q+2$ candidate entries, from the target-group results plus the received generator and published $\mathsf K^\alpha$.
Their total with the comparisons is at most $N_{\mathrm{cmp}}(u)$ since $u=2Q+2$ and $\sum_{j=1}^Q(L+3j-1)+Q+2\le uL+u(u+1)/2$.
Taking the union bound gives the stated charge estimate conditional on the symbolic transcript, since $Q\le u$.
The estimate holds unconditionally because the bound is independent of that transcript.

In a lazy exposure of $\mathsf R_\$$ with images unrevealed, every assigned target-group label before a first mark has an entry by (M1)–(M3).
At most $2+3Q$ target-group strings have been examined, from those two initial elements and at most three examinations per call.
If a query can set a first guess mark, the target exponent has no assigned label, since the mark requires no entry.
The number of unexamined strings is at least $N_{\mathsf{free}}>0$ by the label cap in (P2) and $Q<2^\lambda$.
Condition on the encryption coins, the non-label randomness and the prior table decisions, which determine the query string.
If the target exponent is unassigned, uniformity of the remaining injection then gives query-hit probability at most $1/N_{\mathsf{free}}$.
A union bound over at most $2^\lambda$ key queries gives the stated guess bound.
add.explain: Transfer both first-mark probabilities by one message-mask coupling, then use two exposure orders of the same injections.

add.label: Sparse trimmed fibers
add.name: Triangular projection and box bound for trimmed fibers
add.statement:
Let $\Theta \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^I$, with $|I| \le N$, be a lattice of rank $d \in [3]$ with a basis matrix $B$, $F$ a nonempty set of box points on $I \cup \{i'\}$, $i' \notin I$, trimmed by $\Theta$, and $\Phi(r) := (B^\top r_I, r_{i'})$.

 
(a) If $\dim \Phi(F) = d + 1$ and $\Phi(F)$ is in a coset of a subgroup of index $q$ of $\mathbb{Z}^{d+1}$, then $\Pr[F] \le \Lambda_d\, g^d\, h(\Theta)\, m(\Theta)/q$.
(b) If $F^\perp$ has a rank $d'$ with $1 \le d' < d$ and a largest minor at a set $J \subseteq I$, and the restriction to $I$ of each vector of $F^\perp$ lies in $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}(\Theta)$, then $\Pr[F]\, h(F^\perp) \le \Lambda_{d-d'}\, g^{d-d'}\, h(\Theta)\, m(\Theta)$. In the proof, $y=(y_1,y_2)=B^\top r_I$ is split according to $B=(B_1,B_2)$, and $\mathbb B^I$ denotes the Euclidean unit ball on the coordinates $I$.
add.proof:
For a fixed image pair $(y,x)$ with $x=r_{i'}$ its box density is at most $m(\Theta)/g$, by fixing the new coordinate and counting a fiber of the other coordinates.
Thus $\Pr[F]\le m(\Theta)|\Phi(F)|/g$.
In (a) use $d'=0$, $J=\varnothing$, $k=d+1$, $a=1$, and let $p$ be the identity with index $\delta=q$.
In (b), the matrix $B_J$ has rank $d'$ since its column span contains the invertible largest-minor block $Y_J$ of a basis $Y$ of $F^\perp$.
Extend a basis of the saturated integer kernel of $B_J$ to a basis of the coefficient lattice $\mathbb Z^d$ by the basis-extension demand.
In the corresponding basis $B=(B_1,B_2)$ the $k-1$ columns of $B_2$ vanish on $J$, with $k=d+1-d'$.
This basis change preserves the fibers up to an invertible change of their image coordinates.
It preserves all absolute full minors because the basis change has determinant of absolute value one.
With $z=B^\top r_I-y_\Theta$, substituting $BU$ into the trimming quadratic gives $(U^\top z)^\top(U^\top\Sigma_\Theta U)^{-1}(U^\top z)=z^\top\Sigma_\Theta^{-1}z$.
The map $(u,t)\mapsto(Bu,t)$ sends the real normal space of $\Phi(F)$ isomorphically onto that of $F$ by the assumed restriction on $F^\perp$.
Thus $\Phi(F)$ has affine dimension $k$.
Take an integer normal basis matrix $V$ of $\Phi(F)$ with blocks $V_1,V_2,V_3$ of $d'$, $k-1$, and one rows.
The pullback of its columns is $YC$ with $C$ a nonsingular integer matrix, because they are independent integer normals of $F$.
Restricting this matrix equation to $J$ gives $(B_1)_J V_1=Y_J C$.
Taking absolute determinants yields $a\delta\ge h(F^\perp)>0$ for $a=|\det(B_1)_J|$ and $\delta=|\det V_1|$.
The projection $p$ to the last $k$ coordinates is injective on the affine span of $\Phi(F)$ because $V_1$ is nonsingular.
The projected integer kernel of $V^\top$ is the kernel of $(y_2,x)\mapsto V_2^\top y_2+V_3^\top x$ modulo $V_1^\top\mathbb Z^{d'}$.
That map is surjective by the transpose-surjectivity demand for the saturated normal lattice of $\Phi(F)$.
Thus the projection lies in a coset of a subgroup of index $\delta$.
In either case $p(\Phi(F))$ has affine dimension $k$ and the same cardinality as $\Phi(F)$.
Its convex hull contains a lattice simplex of volume at least $\delta/k!$ by the determinant formula.
For hull volume $V_*$, applying the lattice-point bound after mapping the coset to $\mathbb Z^k$ gives $|\Phi(F)|\le k! V_*/\delta+k$.
As $V_*\ge\delta/k!$, this is at most $(k+1)!V_*/\delta$.
The projected trimming region is contained in the product of the last-coordinate interval and a translate of $(R_{\mathrm{tr}}g/\sqrt{12})B_2^\top\mathbb B^I$ by the covariance formula, where $B_2=B$ in (a).
By singular-value decomposition this bounds $V_*$ by $g(2R_{\mathrm{tr}}g/\sqrt{12})^{k-1}\sqrt{\det(B_2^\top B_2)}$, using the unit cube to bound the unit ball in dimension $k-1$.
The inequality $a\sqrt{\det(B_2^\top B_2)}\le h(\Theta)\sqrt{\binom N{k-1}}$ follows from Cauchy–Binet, using rows outside $J$, whose scaled minors are full minors of $B$ after adjoining $J$.
Consequently $a\delta\Pr[F]$ is at most $g^{k-1}h(\Theta)m(\Theta)$ times $(k+1)!(2R_{\mathrm{tr}})^{k-1}\sqrt{\binom{N}{k-1}/12^{k-1}}$.
The bound $\binom N m\le N^m/m!$ gives coefficients at most $2\sqrt3$, $4\sqrt2$, and $20\sqrt2/3$ multiplying $(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\sqrt N)^m$ for $m=k-1=1,2,3$ respectively.
These three estimates are bounded by $\Lambda_{k-1}$ in the respective cases by (I3).
Substitute $a=1,\delta=q$ in (a) and $a\delta\ge h(F^\perp)$ in (b) to obtain the bounds.
add.explain: Use a projected box instead of the exact projected ellipsoid volume.

edges.demand: The square Moore matrix with rows (β, β^q, …, β^(q^(d−1))) for d entries β linearly independent over F_q has nonzero determinant.
Sampling the reduction's coins before the run changes no output.
T_(LIFT) is polynomial in N and log q.
The gradient of a computation costs a constant number of operations per operation of the computation.

At every fixed r, formally distinct source-group expressions coincide with probability at most ε_f, and a target-group nonidentity with multiple χκ has coincidence probability at most ε_f. Every r giving an identity lies in the fiber of the mark stack and its vectors u_c. For a target-group comparison of a formally distinct pair or a key comparison with χ=1, an identity at fixed r has a nonzero mark stack because zero stacks force formal equality with χ=0.

With ϖ=Ω_22 ζ ζ′ ζ″ ε, the cleared target-group comparison with χκ and the cleared difference of source-group expressions are polynomials of total degree at most d_f=3D+2n+2K_1+6 in the ordinary coins and r.
The zero probability of a nonzero comparison polynomial of degree at most d_f+1, evaluated on independent uniform coordinates each with at least q−D choices, is at most (d_f+1)/(q−D).
Lazy sampling of the label maps couples the symbolic and real generic-group simulations up to the first collision.
V^⊤Z^(d+1) = Z^(d′) for the saturated normal lattice.
A basis of a saturated sublattice of Z^d extends to a basis of Z^d.
